description: The provided image is a donut-style pie chart from the paper “Can Language Models Follow Multiple Turns of Entangled Instructions,” visually representing the distribution of scores across ten distinct capabilities evaluated in the study. The chart is divided into ten colored segments, each labeled with a capability and its corresponding numerical score. Starting from the top and moving clockwise: “Prioritization” (100, light red), “Triggering” (100, light blue), “Recursive Reasoning” (110, medium blue), “Dynamic Environment” (100, dark blue), “Memorization” (100, light teal), “Dynamic Instruction” (100, medium teal), “Multitasking” (160, green), “Privacy Protection” (111, red), “Personalization” (100, orange-red), and “Contradiction Resolution” (100, brownish-red). The inner ring of the donut is segmented into three thematic categories — “Contradiction Resolution,” “Context Tracking,” and “Context Retrieving” — each encompassing a subset of the outer capabilities, suggesting a conceptual grouping of related skills. The scores are not percentages but absolute values, with “Multitasking” scoring highest at 160 and “Contradiction Resolution” and “Prioritization” among the lowest at 100. The chart uses color coding and radial layout to emphasize relative performance, with no explicit legend but clear labeling via leader lines. The visual design implies a comparative assessment of language model capabilities across complex, multi-turn instruction-following tasks.
